summary.headline: Gulf Oil Q4 FY26 posted record quarter: 45,000 KL lubricant volume (+14%), EBITDA INR 135 crore, FY26 revenue above INR 4,000 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly volume, revenue and EBITDA for Q4 FY26, with lubricant volume up about 14% and revenue up about 14%. FY26 lubricant volume grew 10.5% to 1,68,000 KL, and consolidated revenue crossed INR 4,000 crore for the first time. Margin pressure is building from the Middle East crisis and rupee depreciation, with crude moving from about USD 65-70 in February to USD 90-120 in March onward. Management is prioritising supply security and per-litre price pass-through, and is holding its 12-14% EBITDA margin band as the target. The Board recommended a record FY26 dividend of INR 51 per share, including a INR 30 final.

segments.name: Passenger car motor oils
segments.commentary: Delivered double-digit growth in Q4; management wants to grow faster here given lower market share.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Double-digit growth in Q4; all vehicle categories reported positive growth in FY26.

segments.name: OEM franchisee workshops / B2B industrial
segments.commentary: Strong double-digit growth across 40+ OEM partnerships (management cites 50-55 OEMs); industrial growing consistently at double digits.

segments.name: Tirex (EV charging subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Crossed INR 100 crore revenue in FY26; holds at least 35-40% share of new bus DC charger orders; supplies MG Motors and VinFast for AC chargers. Stake raised from 51% to 65% for INR 38 crore; new plant due Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Lubricant volume growth targeted at 2-3x industry; industry growth assumed about 3-4% (Systematix cited 8-9% industry).
EBITDA margin band of 12-14% to be protected; management said 14-16% is a challenge in the current environment.
Chennai capacity expansion expected Q3 FY27 and Silvassa expansion Q4 FY27; management said timelines are on track.
Distribution growth target of 10-15% in both urban and rural areas.
Tirex new plant expected to be operational in Q3 FY27; funding via a mix of equity and borrowings.
Margins may move toward the lower or higher end of the band as realisations rise sharply.
capex_capacity: Chennai plant capacity expansion on track; expected to come on stream first, targeted by Q3 FY27.
Silvassa plant expansion on track; civil work under way, targeted by Q4 FY27.
Tirex building a new plant, expected to be running in Q3 FY27; funded by equity and borrowings plus working capital.
Tirex stake raised from 51% to 65% in FY26 for INR 38 crore.
Base oil stock held at 45-60 days (normal 45 days), raised by 10-15 days for supply security.
demand_pricing: Demand robust across segments; March-end saw extra demand partly from supply-security buying by OEMs and channel. Management says Jan-Feb also grew double digit.
Management said the channel stocking effect was real but not the whole story, with demand continuing into April-May.
Multiple price increases taken in response to crude and input costs; management says input costs now reprice in 1-2 weeks versus about 2 months earlier.
Base oil sourced mainly from South Korea and Singapore refiners; allocation of 80-90% received from some refiners. No major supply disruption so far.
Management says price increases are being passed through per litre, though percentage margin may fluctuate.
Management declined to quantify Castrol's like-for-like price premium, and said it cannot know Castrol's base oil procurement advantage.

Data centre cooling: two products (PAO-based synthetic and mineral-based) developed and made in India; material compatibility tests done, data-centre trials next. Management says volume will be small.

qa_highlights.question: What strategic levers are prioritised for FY27 in lubricants, OEM partnerships and EV-ready fluids?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing segment-wise focus under 'Unlock 2.0' (accelerate, premiumise, transform), with digital initiatives, mechanic outreach and EV fluids for more than 30 OEMs. It aims to grow margins through premium products.

qa_highlights.question: What capital allocation and risk framework applies to dividends, R&D, hedging and liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: Global R&D is funded by Gulf globally, so no direct P&L hit in India. Payout was lifted from 30-40% three to four years ago to c.72% for FY26, as cash builds and M&A and Tirex funding are still ahead.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Chennai and Silvassa expansions on schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Chennai is expected by Q3 and Silvassa by Q4 FY27; civil work at Silvassa is progressing.

qa_highlights.question: Are base oil availability and price rises hitting margins in Q1-Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to hold the 12-14% margin band and has cost levers. Supply has held so far, but a prolonged crisis could squeeze refiner supply chains. Prices are being raised repeatedly.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 volume driven by channel stocking or sustainable demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said double-digit growth ran through the year, with March-end boosted by supply-security buying from OEMs and distributors. Demand remains good into April-May.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook and revenue timing for data-centre cooling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume will be low and timing depends on which data centres are targeted; no revenue timing given.

risks_watch: Crude and base oil price volatility: crude moved from USD 65-70 to USD 90-120; margin band of 12-14% at risk if pass-through lags.
Supply: about 50% of base oil is imported from Korea, Singapore and the Middle East; a prolonged crisis could tighten refiner allocations (currently 80-90%).
Rupee depreciation keeping input costs elevated.
Tirex: bus-segment growth below expectation; new plant and working capital needs require funding via equity and borrowings.
Data-centre cooling products: commercial timing and volume undisclosed; management says volume will be small.
Brand and pricing: management declined to quantify Castrol's premium; the gap in EBITDA margin versus the market leader remains wide.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and demand, with a strong Q4 and FY26 record. Cautious on margins and supply, with management repeatedly calling the situation volatile and declining to quantify the Castrol premium or the price hike.
key_quotes: Extremely delighted to share with you that Q4 has been a record quarter for us in terms of our volumes, revenues and EBITDA.
And I think all the actions are being taken to ensure supplies to our customers and consumers because our customers should not suffer.
I think ensuring supply security is the most critical part, and pricing is the secondary thing.
So overall, we have been a cash generating company.
